course_description:
This course builds upon Foundations of Property Law but focuses exclusively on property rights and interests, both legal and equitable.

LAWS2707 (Interests in Property) builds on LAWS2706 (Foundations in Property Law) and focuses on distinct legal and equitable interests in property, primarily (but not exclusively) real property. The course comprises six main topics:

The Maria De Donatis Memorial Prize in Corporate Law: ﾠ The female student with the highest overall marks in their first attempt at LAWS2706, LAWS2707 and LAWS3702 will be recommended for this prize.

The Walter Harrison Prizes (Prize 1): ﾠ The student with the highest marks for the first attempt at Foundations of Property Law and Interests in Property will be recommended for this prize.

UQ Corrs Chambers Westgarth Internships: The student with the highest mark in their first attempt at LAWS2707 will be recommended to Corrs Westgarth's Real Estate Team for a paid internship.

course_aims:
Education Mission Statement

The mission of the School of Law is to educate you in and about the law. We seek to assist you to think critically about the law and to investigate its structures, principles, policies, and values. This is achieved by engaging with you as fellow investigators in a range of critical and intellectual conversations about the law and its place in society. Our role is thus to guide you in your own intellectual journey in the law and to equip you with the necessary skills that will enable you to continue that journey long after you have left the School.

Course Aims

The broad aims of the course are to provide:

learning_outcomes.description: Identify and recall the principles and rules of property law.
Identify and apply property law principles in analysing particular factual situation.
Analyse and interpret relevant case law and statutes relating to property.
Demonstrate skills in written communication (including organising and structuring ideas) in the context of providing advice on legal issues related to property law.
Collaborate in a team to analyse property law issues, provide legal advice and reflect on professional practices.

assessment_summary.title: Partner Briefing: Revised Legal Analysis and Advice

assessment_details.title: Memorandum of Advice
assessment_details.task_description: Your team will produce a 1,500 word ±10% (excluding footnotes, headnote and recommendations) memorandum of advice addressed to the partner at Corrs Chambers Westgarth, advising on the legal issues arising from the Thornfield Commons scenario. The memorandum should: identify and define the key legal issues arising from the scenario; apply the relevant property law principles, case law and statute; develop clear, well-reasoned legal advice and specific recommendations; and be formatted as a professional legal memorandum addressed to a senior partner of Corrs Chambers Westgarth. Format: 12-point Arial or Times New Roman font, 1.5 line spacing, with appropriate headings. All citations must comply with AGLC4 . Read full task description Hide full task description
assessment_details.assessment_security: Open assessment: In this assessment you can use resources such as your notes, course materials, and other tools, including AI, while completing the task. The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.

All submissions are made through Cadmus (via Blackboard). For this team assessment piece, one member submits on behalf of the group. However, all team members must review and agree on the final version before any submissions. Each student is responsible for submitting their own individual components to the team's final submission.

assessment_details.task_description: Your team must record and submit an 8–10 minute video simulating an internal team meeting responding to the new facts. In the discussion, your team should: analyse how the new facts change or affect your original legal reasoning and recommendations; provide revised legal advice and recommendations; and use professional oral communication appropriate for a work context. Your discussion should focus on demonstrating your team’s legal reasoning, adaptability, and collaborative decision-making rather than delivering a scripted presentation. assessment_details.title: Reflection
assessment_details.task_description: You will individually reflect (400-500 words) on your learning and professional development working in a team to solve a legal scenario. Your reflection should: Analyse your personal and team contributions by drawing on: your experiences completing the task; how you enacted professional, personal, and/or institutional values ; and evidence from your progress checks (i.e., sentiment checks, self- and/or peer evaluation), to produce insights into how you have grown as a developing legal professional (e.g. legal reasoning, communication, collaboration). Format: Formal written reflection. Use 12-point Arial or Times New Roman font and 1.5 line spacing. First person language is appropriate. Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.topic: Co-ownership Lecture on the basic concepts of co-ownership; joint tenancies versus tenancies in common; determination of co-ownership. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Community Titles and Body Corporate I Lecture on the history of strata title schemes, key concepts of BCCMA, establishing a community titles scheme, types of community titles scheme, Community Management Statements. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Co-ownership Tutorial exercise based on material from Week 1. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Community Title Schemes and Body Corporates II Lecture on lots and lot owners, the Body Corporate governance of community titles schemes, dispute resolution, termination of a community titles scheme. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Community Title Schemes and Body Corporate I Tutorial exercise based on material from Week 2. Please attend another tutorial this week if your tutorial falls on the Public Holiday (12 August). Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Leasehold Interests in Land I The lecture will introduce students to the course and the "lease" versus "licence" distinction, the elements and types of leases, as well as the creation of leasehold interests in land (including formalities). Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Community Title Schemes and Body Corporates II The tutorial is based on material from Week 3. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Leasehold Interest in Land II The lecture will examine covenants for the lessee and lessor, assignment of leases and the privily of contract and estate. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Leasehold Interest in Land I Tutorial based on content from Week 4. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Leasehold Interest in Land III The lecture will examine the termination of leases (including forfeiture and relief against forfeiture), and a overview of retail shop leases. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Leasehold Interest in Land II Tutorial based on content from Week 5. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Easements and Other Covenants Lecture on essential characteristics of easements, creation and enforcement of easements, extinguishment of easements, profits à prendre, statutory covenants. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Leasehold Interests in Land III The Tutorial will be based on material from Week 6. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Native Title I Lecture on history of native title in Australia (including Mabo litigation); native title and the common law. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Easements The Tutorial will be based on material from Week 7. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Native Title II Lecture on Native Title Act 1993 (Cth) (including proof and claim procedures, extinguishment, validation and confirmation of extinguishment, the "future acts" regime, and Indigenous Land Use Agreements). Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Native Title I The Tutorial will be based on material from Week 8. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Security Interests in Property I Lecture on introduction to security interests generally; security interests over land (primarily land mortgages); nature and types of land mortgages (legal and equitable); creation and contents of land mortgages. Since Monday, 5 October 2026, is a public holiday, this week's lecture will be recorded and uploaded directly to Blackboard . Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
No Tutorial
Security Interests II Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Native Title II Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Security Interests III Lecture on security interests over personal property (post-PPSA). Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Security Interests in Property I & II The Tutorial will be based on material from Week 10 & 11. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
